pitch: An invented kernel compiler bridges tiny/1 cases to byte programs; a separate reference compiler handles Fibonacci. Pair evidence never grants compiler-wide correctness.

showcase.check: Run the source, compiled program, metered adapter, and invented interpreter at x0=10.
showcase.prompt: For the tiny/1 source Code<op (x0) = rec r0(v0, v1, v2) = if is_zero(v0) then v1 else r0(sub(v0, 1), v2, add(v1, v2)) measure fuel in r0(x0, 0, 1)>, The untrusted reference ~compile target is n=256, code bytes at address 0: [2, 58, 3, 59, 1, 0, 3, 60, 1, 1, 3, 61, 2, 59, 7, 18, 6, 22, 2, 60, 6, 56, 2, 59, 8, 255, 3, 62, 2, 61, 3, 63, 2, 60, 3, 64, 2, 61, 4, 64, 3, 65, 2, 62, 3, 59, 2, 63, 3, 60, 2, 65, 3, 61, 6, 12, 0, 0]; input x0 is stored at address 58; all other cells are 0 initially. Instructions are pairs (opcode, operand): 0 HALT, 1 LDI, 2 LD, 3 ST, 4 ADD, 5 SUB, 6 JMP, 7 JZ, 8 ADDI. Arithmetic is modulo 256. Each executed pair, including HALT, costs one machine step. Run with x0=10, fuel=500; give the exact integer source result, byte-machine result, machine steps and metered run_prog steps. The invented vn_interp has the verified cost 499*x0+242 layer-0 steps for this program on x0=0..13, and the source has 3*x0+1 steps. Give these two costs too.
showcase.why_hard: Every vn/1 instruction expands into multiple integer and list operations.

showcase.check: Validate every singleton x0 in 0..15 at fuel=500.
showcase.prompt: For tiny/1 source Code<op (x0) = rec r0(v0, v1, v2) = if is_zero(v0) then v1 else r0(sub(v0, 1), v2, add(v1, v2)) measure fuel in r0(x0, 0, 1)>, The untrusted reference ~compile target is n=256, code bytes at address 0: [2, 58, 3, 59, 1, 0, 3, 60, 1, 1, 3, 61, 2, 59, 7, 18, 6, 22, 2, 60, 6, 56, 2, 59, 8, 255, 3, 62, 2, 61, 3, 63, 2, 60, 3, 64, 2, 61, 4, 64, 3, 65, 2, 62, 3, 59, 2, 63, 3, 60, 2, 65, 3, 61, 6, 12, 0, 0]; input x0 is stored at address 58; all other cells are 0 initially. Instructions are pairs (opcode, operand): 0 HALT, 1 LDI, 2 LD, 3 ST, 4 ADD, 5 SUB, 6 JMP, 7 JZ, 8 ADDI. Arithmetic is modulo 256. Each executed pair, including HALT, costs one machine step. For each x0=0..15, the source uses exact integers but an output outside 0..255 becomes Bottom(overflow); the target returns the final byte accumulator at HALT. With fuel=500 does this source/target pair commute? List all mismatches.
showcase.why_hard: Exact integer Fibonacci eventually exceeds the byte accumulator.

showcase.check: Compile every rate k and validate all 16 inputs in ascending order.
showcase.prompt: In the reference ~compile tiny/1 source Code<op (x0) = rec r0(v0, v1) = if is_zero(v0) then v1 else r0(sub(v0, 1), add(v1, sub(7, x0))) measure fuel in r0(x0, 0)>, replace the rate literal 7 in sub(7, x0) with k. The target's HALT accumulator is (x0*(k-x0)) modulo 256 on x0=0..15; n=256, fuel=500; all other cells are 0 initially. The source's exact integer result outside 0..255 is Bottom(overflow). Find ALL k in 0..255 for which this source/target pair agrees on every x0.
showcase.why_hard: The answer requires exhaustive translation validation of 256 distinct routines.

story.ascii: op exec_one(mem: list, a: int, pc: int, arg3: int) -> list = let operand = list_get(mem, mod(add(pc, 1), list_len(mem))) in case { eq(op, 0) -> list_set(list_set_list(list_set(list <items: 0, list <items>, 0>, 0, a), 1, mem), 2, pc); else -> case { eq(op, 1) -> list_set(list_set_list(list_set(list <items: 0, list <items>, 0>, 0, operand), 1, mem), 2, mod(add(pc, 2), list_len(mem))); else -> case { eq(op, 2) -> list_set(list_set_list(list_set(list <items: 0, list <items>, 0>, 0, list_get(mem, mod(operand, list_len(mem)))), 1, mem), 2, mod(add(pc, 2), list_len(mem))); else -> case { eq(op, 3) -> list_set(list_set_list(list_set(list <items: 0, list <items>, 0>, 0, a), 1, list_set(mem, mod(operand, list_len(mem)), a)), 2, mod(add(pc, 2), list_len(mem))); else -> case { eq(op, 4) -> list_set(list_set_list(list_set(list <items: 0, list <items>, 0>, 0, mod(add(a, list_get(mem, mod(operand, list_len(mem)))), 256)), 1, mem), 2, mod(add(pc, 2), list_len(mem))); else -> case { eq(op, 5) -> list_set(list_set_list(list_set(list <items: 0, list <items>, 0>, 0, mod(sub(a, list_get(mem, mod(operand, list_len(mem)))), 256)), 1, mem), 2, mod(add(pc, 2), list_len(mem))); else -> case { eq(op, 6) -> list_set(list_set_list(list_set(list <items: 0, list <items>, 0>, 0, a), 1, mem), 2, mod(operand, list_len(mem))); else -> case { eq(op, 7) -> case { is_zero(a) -> list_set(list_set_list(list_set(list <items: 0, list <items>, 0>, 0, a), 1, mem), 2, mod(operand, list_len(mem))); else -> list_set(list_set_list(list_set(list <items: 0, list <items>, 0>, 0, a), 1, mem), 2, mod(add(pc, 2), list_len(mem))) }; else -> case { eq(op, 8) -> list_set(list_set_list(list_set(list <items: 0, list <items>, 0>, 0, mod(add(a, operand), 256)), 1, mem), 2, mod(add(pc, 2), list_len(mem))); else -> fail_illegal() } } } } } } } } } L1

story.ascii: op compile_expr(expr: expr, names: list, slots: list, depth: int, lets: int, pc: int) -> list = rec walk(expr, names, slots, depth, lets, pc) = case { lt(depth, 12) -> case { str_eq(tag_of(expr), "var") -> emit(2, lookup(field(expr, 0), names, slots)); else -> case { str_eq(tag_of(expr), "lit") -> case { lt(-1, field(expr, 0)) -> case { lt(field(expr, 0), 256) -> emit(1, field(expr, 0)); else -> unsupported() }; else -> unsupported() }; else -> case { str_eq(tag_of(expr), "call") -> case { eq(len(field(expr, 1)), 2) -> case { str_eq(field(expr, 0), "add") -> let left = walk(get(field(expr, 1), 0), names, slots, depth, lets, pc) in let right_pc = add(pc, add(len(left), 2)) in let right = walk(get(field(expr, 1), 1), names, slots, add(depth, 1), lets, right_pc) in concat(left, concat(emit(3, add(48, depth)), concat(right, emit(4, add(48, depth))))); else -> case { str_eq(field(expr, 0), "sub") -> case { lt(depth, 11) -> let left = walk(get(field(expr, 1), 0), names, slots, depth, lets, pc) in let right_pc = add(pc, add(len(left), 2)) in let right = walk(get(field(expr, 1), 1), names, slots, add(depth, 1), lets, right_pc) in concat(left, concat(emit(3, add(48, depth)), concat(right, concat(emit(3, add(48, add(depth, 1))), concat(emit(2, add(48, depth)), emit(5, add(48, add(depth, 1)))))))); else -> unsupported() }; else -> unsupported() } }; else -> unsupported() }; else -> case { str_eq(tag_of(expr), "let") -> case { lt(lets, 6) -> let value = walk(field(expr, 1), names, slots, depth, lets, pc) in concat(value, concat(emit(3, add(48, depth)), walk(field(expr, 2), append(names, field(expr, 0)), append(slots, add(48, depth)), add(depth, 1), add(lets, 1), add(pc, add(len(value), 2))))); else -> unsupported() }; else -> case { str_eq(tag_of(expr), "case") -> case { str_eq(tag_of(field(expr, 1)), "some") -> case { lt(0, len(field(expr, 0))) -> rec arms_walk(arms, arm_pc) = case { eq(len(arms), 0) -> walk(field(field(expr, 1), 0), names, slots, depth, lets, arm_pc); else -> let arm = get(arms, 0) in case { case { str_eq(tag_of(field(arm, 0)), "test") -> case { str_eq(tag_of(field(field(arm, 0), 0)), "call") -> case { str_eq(field(field(field(arm, 0), 0), 0), "is_zero") -> eq(len(field(field(field(arm, 0), 0), 1)), 1); else -> false }; else -> false }; else -> false } -> let test_code = walk(get(field(field(field(arm, 0), 0), 1), 0), names, slots, depth, lets, arm_pc) in let rest_pc = add(arm_pc, add(len(test_code), 2)) in let rest = arms_walk(tail(arms), rest_pc) in let body_pc = add(rest_pc, add(len(rest), 2)) in branch(test_code, rest, walk(field(arm, 1), names, slots, depth, lets, body_pc), arm_pc); else -> unsupported() } } measure len(arms) on (field(expr, 0), pc); else -> unsupported() }; else -> unsupported() }; else -> unsupported() } } } } }; else -> unsupported() } measure size(expr) on (expr, names, slots, depth, lets, pc) L3
